pairs.difference: A: the scarf fills the middle of the card, from the knot at upper centre down to the tails near the bottom edge, and reads at once as a neckerchief. B: the lasso is a thin, flat loop-and-coil lying in the upper-middle band (area 0.117, under the real minimum of 0.198). Wide purple bands are left empty above and below it, and at thumbnail size it reads as a squiggle, not a lasso.
pairs.fix: Draw the coiled lasso big and chunky, tilted three-quarters toward the viewer, filling most of the card from near the top edge to near the bottom edge, with the open loop swinging toward one corner.

pairs.difference: A: the boot is shown in strict side profile, pushed to the left half, with a large empty orange area at upper right and right. It sits at the bottom of the real area range (0.204). B: the mortarboard is slightly turned and centred. It is wide and flat (height 0.506) but still reads instantly. This is a weak call: B's flat height is also outside the real range.
pairs.fix: Turn the cowboy boot three-quarters toward the viewer, slightly tilted, and scale it up so the toe reaches near the right edge and the shaft reaches near the top edge, filling the card.

pairs.difference: A: the computer on the desk matches the real card in the lessons, angled three-quarters and cropped by the desk at the bottom. B: the saddle is dead-centre and seen straight-on and symmetric. A flat horizontal rail runs edge to edge behind it, cutting the card in half, and the stirrups hang straight down into empty blue.
pairs.fix: Show the saddle three-quarters from the side and slightly from above, resting on a short angled fence rail that goes out of frame at one corner instead of a flat bar across the whole card. Let the saddle fill most of the card.

pairs.difference: A: the open book sits low on a table, cropped at the left edge, with a railing and a cropped plant pot at upper right. It is a busy scene, but the book is the clear hero. B: the stack of maps fills the card edge to edge (area 0.51, above the real maximum of 0.442). It is a tilted fan of three near-identical sheets, so the first read is 'paper stack', not a single map. Weak call.
pairs.fix: Draw one folded treasure map, slightly tilted, filling about two-thirds of the card with a little background visible on every side, with the X mark large near the centre.

pairs.difference: A: the chest is angled three-quarters with its lid open, filling the card down to the sand, with shell and coins in the bottom corners. B: the barrel stands upright, dead-centre and front-on, like a symmetric column (width 0.581, below the real range). There are even bands of empty wall and floor on both sides.
pairs.fix: Turn the barrel three-quarters and tip it slightly, or show it at an angle from above. Make it larger so it reaches close to the left and right edges, and add a small prop at its base.

pairs.difference: A: the locomotive is fully contained and centred, with an even band of desert sky above. The tracks run to the bottom corners, and the whole object sits safely inside the frame. B: the coaster cars sweep in an arc that is cropped by the top and bottom edges, the dynamic, edge-touching framing the real cards show. Weak call.
pairs.fix: Push the locomotive closer and lower so the cowcatcher nearly touches the bottom-left corner and the smokestack nearly touches the top edge, with the tender cut off by the right edge.

pairs.difference: A: the popcorn cart is angled three-quarters and fills the card from the awning near the top to the wheels near the bottom. B: the cactus is a straight-on, symmetric saguaro set dead-centre (width 0.502, below the real minimum of 0.661; margin 0.119, above the real maximum of 0.098), with empty sand and orange around it on all sides.
pairs.fix: Make the cactus much larger and turn it slightly, so its arms reach near the left and right edges. Tilt the view a little from above so the sand base shows depth.

pairs.difference: A: the saloon-door frame is a thin, open rectangle, mostly see-through to the pink wall. It is centred, with little solid mass, so at thumbnail size it reads as a thin outline. B: the sneakers sit low (height 0.487) with an empty orange top half, but they are bold, solid shapes and read instantly. Weak call.
pairs.fix: Draw the swinging saloon doors close-up and three-quarter turned, with the two door leaves large and solid, filling most of the card. Crop the posts at the top and bottom edges.

pairs.difference: A: the ring box is tilted three-quarters with its lid open, and the coin faces the viewer, filling the card. B: the sheriff star is a flat, front-on, symmetric star in the exact centre (area 0.189, below the real minimum of 0.198). Its thin points with ball tips leave lots of purple between them, and it sits on a centred sunburst.
pairs.fix: Tilt the sheriff star in three-quarter view so its thickness shows, make it larger so its points nearly touch the edges, and fatten the star's body.

pairs.difference: A: the rowboat is diagonal and close-up, with the dock cropped at the top-left edge, filling the card. B: the covered wagon is small (area 0.22) in the upper middle. A wide empty dirt road takes the lower third, the tongue points off to the lower right, and the whole scene is landscape, not object.
pairs.fix: Bring the covered wagon much closer, turned three-quarters, so the canvas top nearly touches the top edge and the big wheel fills the lower left. Crop the road and sky to thin strips.

pairs.difference: A: the lion statue on its plinth fills the card, slightly turned, with the garden path behind. B: the wall AC unit is wide and flat (height 0.373) across the upper middle, with blue air streaks below. Both read instantly and both look like the real framings, so composition gives no clear reason to pick one.

A: the scout jacket is turned three-quarters, with its sleeves reaching near the left and right edges, filling the card. B: the cowboy hat is front-on, symmetric and dead-centre. It is a wide, flat shape (height 0.465, below the real minimum of 0.581) with large empty blue bands above and below it.
pairs.fix: Show the cowboy hat three-quarters from above and tilted, so the crown and the inside of the brim both show. Make it larger so the brim nearly touches the side edges and the hat fills more of the card's height.

pattern: Generated cards put the hero dead-centre, front-on and symmetric, fully inside the frame with even empty bands around it. The real cards turn the object three-quarters, tilt it, and push it to or past the edges. The generated western items are often too narrow or too flat (the cactus, barrel and star are too narrow; the hat, lasso and mortarboard too flat), so the card reads as empty background with a small icon instead of a filled, dynamic object.
